Hi Aisha —

Thanks for pulling this together and sharing Tideware’s matrix. Quick read-through and our initial position below (happy to iterate):

Exclusion categories (Redwood position):
- Scheduled maintenance: excluded if we provide >=48 hours notice and maintenance window > 2 hours. Short, opportunistic patching (<2 hours) will count toward uptime.
- Customer-initiated downtime (e.g., planned cutover where customer asks us to pause): excluded if documented via ticket and acknowledged by both sides prior to the window.
- Third-party region failures (cloud provider regional outages): excluded from customer-level uptime if we can show upstream provider RCA that indicates region-wide failure; otherwise we treat as failure for the affected region.
- Force majeure, DDoS caused by external amplification vectors, and customer misuse: excluded by standard definitions in the SLA.

Measurement and credit mechanics (proposed):
- Baseline: 99.95% per-region availability (region = cloud region where customer routes production traffic).
- Credits: tiered, applied to that region’s monthly invoice only — not global aggregate. Example bands we propose:
  * 99.95% <= uptime < 99.90% -> 5% credit
  * 99.90% <= uptime < 99.50% -> 15% credit
  * uptime < 99.50% -> 30% credit
- Calculation method: per-minute unavailability aggregated across the monthly billing window, divided by total minutes the service was expected to be available for that region.
- Monthly cap: we typically cap credits at 45% of the monthly invoice for that region. We’re open to negotiation on the cap but we include it to bound vendor risk.

Reporting and proof: we will provide the automated uptime report (linkable CSV) and an RCA for any incident triggering credit. Credits are applied on the following month’s invoice after mutual acceptance of the RCA.

Action items from us: i) laura/ben to attach sample calculation worked on the draft PDF, ii) please confirm whether Tideware requires a global aggregated view or per-region credits.

If that approach looks reasonable I can have legal draft the specific exclusion language and a deterministic credit formula for the DocuSign flow.

Thanks —

Aisha / Jonas —

Following up with a short note on the measurement math so procurement can validate with finance:

- Measurement window: calendar month UTC.
- Per-region expected minutes = number of days in month * 24 * 60.
- Unavailable minutes = sum of minute-granularity traces where the service returned 5xx or failed health-checks for all active replicas serving that region.
- Uptime % = ((expected minutes - unavailable minutes) / expected minutes) * 100.
- Credit application: multiply the appropriate band % (per Jonas’s table) by the region invoice amount for that month; we post a credit memo to your account.

We’ll include a worked example in the draft SLA (Jonas — I can add a 3-line worked example showing a 17-minute outage in a 30-day month).
